title: An early 31.56-day HD 69830 wave lowers later HIRES error by 25 percent under a fixed activity model
abstract: We test the known and disputed HD 69830 signal with 439 public HIRES exposures on 142 nights. At the original HARPS period of 31.56 days, a wave fitted to the first 85 nights lowers weighted squared error in the next 57 nights by 24.6 percent. The model includes the 8.667-day and 197-day waves, a trend and a linear S-index term. A conditional 30-day block interval is 3.5 to 48.2 percent. Added terms at the reported activity periods retain the gain. Annual terms and season offsets reduce it. With all controls the gain is 14.4 percent and the interval is -2.3 to 31.4 percent. Full-sample amplitudes remain 2.4 to 2.7 m/s. Tests at an updated period give larger gains, but that period can use the same observations. These data support a persistent component under the tested models. They do not prove a planet or exclude activity. The observations were used in earlier work; our contribution is a time transfer test with explicit controls. We include code, original figures, aggregate results, exact input hashes and retrieval steps. External source rows stay outside the baseline bundle.
